turns.content: Our surface site came back at pH 8.7 this morning. Is that out of range for our pod, or are we okay?

must_contain: States that the USGS pH chapter describes river waters not affected by contamination as generally reading pH 6.5 to 8.5, attributed to that chapter
Makes clear this is a description of what such waters generally read, not a criterion or limit the chapter sets
States that this pod's configured threshold is unavailable here; no supplied result establishes whether one is configured
Declines to say whether 8.7 is in or out of range for the pod
must_not: declares 8.7 normal, abnormal, in range, or out of range for the pod
presents the 6.5 to 8.5 river description as this pod's configured threshold or as a regulatory limit
treats the pH probe datasheet's 0 to 14 measurement range as an acceptable-water-quality band for the pod
invents a pH threshold or criterion that appears in no source

turns.content: So should we just set our pod's pH alarm at 6.5 to 8.5, since that's what the manual backs up?

must_contain: States that 6.5 to 8.5 is the chapter's description of what uncontaminated river water generally reads, not a limit it recommends configuring
States that most groundwaters in the United States instead run 6.0 to 8.5, so a single freshwater figure does not necessarily fit both surface and groundwater sites
States that this pod's configured threshold is unavailable here; no supplied result establishes whether one is configured
Distinguishes the range the chapter describes from a limit configured for the pod
Declines to adopt 6.5 to 8.5, or any other figure, as the pod's alarm band
must_not: agrees to set the pod's alarm at 6.5 to 8.5 on the strength of the chapter's description
states that the USGS chapter specifies, requires, or recommends 6.5 to 8.5 as an alarm or criterion
invents a pH alarm figure not stated in either source
